rows.new: Some uses of AI will present ethical issues and may have broad effects on society. Although we have already devoted and will continue to invest significant resources to develop and deploy AI responsibly, the probabilistic nature of AI models means we may not be able to anticipate, identify, or resolve all AI-related issues, deficiencies, and failures before they arise. During model testing, we have sometimes observed unexpected behavior, including autonomous agents taking actions outside of their intended scope. Furthermore, as our AI systems increasingly orchestrate multi-step tasks and interact autonomously with third-party tools, applications, and APIs, errors or misalignments in one component may compound across the workflow, potentially leading to operational, technical, or transactional failures, unauthorized actions, or unforeseen liabilities for us or third parties. In the event of an incident, we may be unable to isolate root causes or detect and respond in a timely manner, and we may face difficulties identifying similar incidents in the future, any of which could subject us to heightened regulatory scrutiny, enforcement actions, or litigation. Unintended consequences, misalignment, misuse, abuse, or customization of our AI tools and systems, which we may not be able to prevent or control, could lead to severe or catastrophic security and societal incidents, or negatively affect human rights, privacy, cybersecurity, employment, public health, or other safety, ethical, and societal interests. Any such occurrences may result in litigation, brand or reputational damage, adverse legislation, increased regulatory scrutiny, orders or requirements to withdraw, retrain, or modify deployed models, and operational shutdowns or injunctions, any of which could harm our business, financial condition, and operating results.

rows.new: We continue to incorporate AI-based features, including AI agents, into our offerings and internal systems. These technologies may introduce novel and unanticipated security threats as our and the market’s understanding of AI-centric risks evolves. In particular, the deployment of and interaction with AI agents presents heightened cybersecurity risks where AI agents may be exploited by malicious actors to facilitate hacking, data exfiltration, privilege escalation, or lateral movement within our systems or the systems of our partners and customers. AI agents may also be vulnerable to prompt injection, adversarial manipulation, or other novel attack vectors that could cause them to bypass access controls, disclose sensitive data, or take unauthorized actions. Furthermore, agentic AI systems that can take actions autonomously may experience model misalignment, fail to work as intended, malfunction, make unintended decisions, or execute multi-step actions without adequate human review, which could lead to accessing systems or executing actions outside their intended scope, data leakage or loss, operational disruption, erroneous transactions, harm to individuals and businesses, cybersecurity incidents, or noncompliance with laws such as the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act or other legal frameworks. In addition, our increasing internal reliance on AI-driven tools and autonomous agents to assist in writing, testing, and deploying software across our production environments and core infrastructure may introduce undetected vulnerabilities, coding errors, or architectural defects that could degrade system reliability or expose us to heightened cybersecurity risks. Because these risks are inherent in emerging and rapidly evolving technology, our existing security frameworks and controls may not fully anticipate, detect, or address them.

 From time to time, others claim we infringe their intellectual property rights, including current copyright infringement and other claims arising from AI training, inference, and output. To resolve these claims, we may enter into royalty-bearing data access or licensing agreements on terms that are less favorable than currently available, stop selling or redesign affected products or services, or pay damages to satisfy indemnification commitments with our customers. Adverse outcomes could also include monetary damages or injunctive relief that may limit or prevent importing, marketing, and selling our products or services that have infringing technologies. We have paid significant amounts to settle claims related to the use of technology and intellectual property rights and to procure intellectual property rights as part of our strategy to manage this risk, and may continue to do so, which could adversely affect our results of operations.

We face risks related to the protection and utilization of our intellectual property that may result in our business and operating results being harmed.
 Protecting our intellectual property rights and combating unlicensed copying and use of our software, source code, trade secrets, and other intellectual property on a global basis is difficult. Similarly, the absence of harmonized patent laws makes it more difficult to ensure consistent respect for patent rights. Use of some third-party technology, such as frontier AI that trains on our interactions with it, could put our intellectual property at risk.
